checklist.step: Rebuild the prohibited-practice inventory from NAIC Model 880 Section 4
actions: Open the Model 880 inventory workbook and create one row per Section 4 sub-part: misrepresentation and false advertising of policy contracts, false information and advertising generally, defamation, boycott/coercion/intimidation, false financial statements, unfair discrimination in life and accident & health rating, rebates and inducements, failure to maintain a complaint record, misrepresentation in applications, failure to maintain marketing and performance records.
For each row name the internal process that can breach it and the owning team (Marketing, Distribution, Pricing, Underwriting, Consumer Affairs, Producer Compliance).
Ask the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager to confirm the process-to-sub-part mapping in writing and paste the reply into the workbook notes column.
Save the workbook as UTPA-inventory-<yyyy> in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Model 880.
checklist.done: every Model 880 Section 4 sub-part has a named internal process, an owning team and a written confirmation from the obligation owner.

checklist.step: Pull the current UTPA statute text for all 51 jurisdictions
actions: For each jurisdiction open the department's statute/regulation library and retrieve the UTPA chapter - representative Alabama Ala. Code tit. 27 ch. 12 on the ALDOI site; supporting Arizona A.R.S. 20-443 et seq., California Ins. Code 790.03, Connecticut C.G.S. 38a-815 et seq.
Print each statute to PDF named <state>-utpa-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and record the last-amended date shown on the source page.
Diff the last-amended date against the date captured in the prior year's file and flag every state that moved.
Search each department's bulletin index for the prior 12 months on the terms rebating, inducement, value-added services, advertising, unfair discrimination and attach any hit to that state's folder.
Hand the list of moved states and new bulletins to the Compliance Analyst as the redraft backlog.
checklist.done: a dated statute capture exists for each of the 51 jurisdictions and every state that amended its UTPA or issued a relevant bulletin is on the redraft backlog.

checklist.step: Refresh the Advertising & Sales Material Review procedure
actions: Rewrite the review procedure to require every piece - print, digital, email, social, agent-produced and lead-vendor material - to enter the review queue in the marketing automation platform before release, tagged with line of business, states of use and intended audience.

Specify the review tests: no misrepresentation of benefits, terms, dividends or the company's financial condition; no comparison of policies without the compared terms; company name and home office city on every piece; no use of a department's name implying endorsement.
Set the advertising file rule: piece id, creator, approval date and reviewer, states of use, media, first and last date used, retained for the exam look-back period.

Write the disapproval and rework path with turnaround targets (3 business days standard, 1 business day for time-critical campaigns) and the escalation to Regulatory Counsel for any comparative or dividend claim.
Circulate the draft to the Marketing Manager for operational feasibility comments and log the responses.
checklist.done: the advertising procedure defines the queue, the review tests, the advertising file fields and the disapproval path, with Marketing's comments logged.

checklist.step: Refresh the Rebating, Inducements & Value-Added Services procedure
actions: State the baseline prohibition from Model 880 Section 4(8): no rebate of premium, no special favour or valuable consideration not stated in the policy, offered by the company or any producer.

Build the state-variation appendix for the 2020 Model 880 value-added services amendment - list, per state, whether value-added services are permitted, the required nexus to the insurance offered, any de minimis dollar cap on gifts and any filing or disclosure precondition.

Define the pre-clearance gate: any producer or marketing offer of goods, services, prizes, charitable donations or fee waivers must be submitted to Market Conduct Compliance with a cost per recipient and a state list before it is offered.
Require the Commission Analyst to confirm that no commission arrangement passes value back to the insured, and record the confirmation each time a new compensation schedule is issued.
Name the record: the inducement clearance register holding offer description, per-recipient value, permitted states, decision, decider and date.
checklist.done: the rebating procedure carries a per-state value-added-services appendix, a pre-clearance gate with a dollar test and a named clearance register.

checklist.step: Refresh the Unfair Discrimination in Rating and Underwriting procedure
actions: Set the rule that no rating factor, eligibility rule, tier assignment or underwriting decline may be based on race, colour, religion, national origin, or on any variable that acts as a proxy for them, and that like risks in like circumstances take like rates.

Require Pricing to submit, for every new or changed rating factor, a variable list with the source data, a proxy-risk assessment and the statistical justification, to Market Conduct Compliance before filing.
Add the model-governance hook: any predictive model or third-party score used in eligibility or pricing must have a documented variable inventory and disparate-impact test before deployment.

Define the periodic look-back: annual review of decline, non-renewal and tier-assignment rates by state and product for unexplained dispersion, with results handed to the Pricing Actuary for explanation.
Write the stop rule - a factor without a submitted justification does not go into a filing, and Market Conduct Compliance holds the release gate.
checklist.done: the procedure names the prohibited bases, the pre-filing justification package, the model-governance hook and the release gate holder.

checklist.step: Refresh the Sales Misrepresentation & Replacement procedure
actions: Require illustrations, benefit summaries and premium quotes given at point of sale to be generated only from approved system-produced templates, with the version stamped on the output.

Set the replacement handling rule: replacement question answered on every application, replacement notice delivered and signed, existing carrier notified within the state's required window, and the replacement register updated.

Define the twisting and churning red flags monitored monthly from the producer management system - replacement rate above peer, first-year lapse above threshold, concentration of surrenders funding new sales.
Route every red-flag producer to Producer Compliance Manager for a file review and record the outcome on the producer record.
State that misrepresentation in an application - by insured or producer - is investigated by SIU and reported into the conduct exception log.
checklist.done: the procedure fixes approved illustration sources, the replacement register, monthly red-flag monitoring and the producer review route.

checklist.step: Refresh the Complaint Record procedure required by Model 880 Section 4(10)
actions: Specify the complaint record fields the model requires: total number of complaints, classification by line of insurance, nature of each complaint, disposition, and the time taken to process each - held for the period since the date of the last market conduct examination.
Define what counts as a complaint (any written expression of dissatisfaction, including department-forwarded, social and email) and forbid case closure without a nature code and a disposition code.

Set the intake service levels: department-forwarded complaints acknowledged within 3 business days and substantively answered inside the state's stated deadline (commonly 15 or 21 calendar days), internal complaints answered within 15 calendar days.
Require the case tool to compute time-to-process in calendar days from receipt to final response and to expose it on the standard complaint register export.
Hand the field list to the Business Systems Analyst so the case tool configuration matches the register export one-for-one.
checklist.done: the complaint record procedure names the mandated fields, the complaint definition, the response clocks and a case-tool configuration that produces the register.

checklist.step: Write the state-variation appendices onto each procedure
actions: For each of the six procedures create a 51-row appendix with columns: jurisdiction, statute cite, deviation from the Model 880 baseline, effective date of the deviation, source PDF filename.
Populate deviations from the dated statute captures and bulletins - for example states that cap gifts, states that require advertising to be filed, states with an expanded discrimination class list.
Leave no row blank: a state with no deviation is written as 'follows Model 880 baseline' with its own cite, never as an empty cell.
Ask Regulatory Counsel to spot-check the ten most-deviating states and initial the appendix rows.
checklist.done: every procedure has a fully populated 51-row appendix with a cite and a source filename on each row.

checklist.step: Take the redrafted set through legal clearance
actions: Read each redrafted procedure against the Model 880 sub-part it claims to cover and confirm every prohibited practice has a controlling instruction.
Check each appendix deviation against the statute capture it cites and reject any statement of law without a cite.
Write a clearance memo listing what was reviewed, what was changed and any residual risk accepted, and date and sign it.
Return unresolved points to the Compliance Analyst with a two-week rework deadline so the 30 April clearance milestone holds.
checklist.done: a dated legal clearance memo covers all six procedures and every appendix statement of law carries a verified cite.

checklist.step: Approve, version and publish the procedure set
actions: Approve each procedure by signing the approval page carrying version number, effective date, next review date (31 May the following year) and the owner name.
Publish the approved PDFs to the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / Model 880 and mark the prior version Superseded rather than deleting it.
Announce the effective date and the material changes to Marketing, Distribution, Pricing, Underwriting, Consumer Affairs and Producer Compliance by a dated notice.
Record the approval in the GRC control record so the annual control shows as performed for the year.
checklist.done: all six procedures are signed, versioned, published with the prior version superseded, and the GRC control record shows the approval date.

checklist.step: Roll the changes into training for staff and appointed producers
actions: Build the assignment population from HRIS job codes touching sales, marketing, underwriting, claims and complaint handling, plus the appointed producer list from the producer management system.

Update the UTPA course content with this year's material changes, especially the value-added-services state grid and any new discrimination class, and set a 10-question assessment with an 80% pass mark.
Assign the course with a 45-day completion window from the effective date and configure automatic reminders at day 15, day 30 and day 40.
Send the non-completion list at day 46 to each manager and to the Producer Compliance Manager for appointment action on producers.
checklist.done: the course is assigned to the full population with reminders configured and a day-46 non-completion escalation issued.

checklist.step: Wire the procedures into operating controls so they bite
actions: Create one GRC control per procedure, each with an owner, a frequency, a test method and a link to the published procedure version.
Map each control up to the Model 880 sub-part and down to the process it sits in so the exam narrative can be produced from the tool.
Set the advertising queue, inducement clearance register, replacement register and complaint register as the named evidence sources for their controls.
Ask the Governance Analyst to confirm no Section 4 sub-part is left without at least one mapped control.
checklist.done: every Model 880 sub-part maps to at least one owned GRC control with a named evidence source.

checklist.step: Run the monthly conduct exception intake
actions: Collect candidate events from four feeds: advertising pieces used without approval, inducement offers made without clearance, complaints coded as misrepresentation or discrimination, and producer red-flag reviews.
Open a conduct exception per event with jurisdiction, Model 880 sub-part, discovery date, affected policyholder count and the business owner.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (procedure gap, training gap, system gap, wilful conduct) and a remediation date no more than 60 days out.
Escalate any wilful-conduct or multi-state event to Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel within one business day for a self-report assessment.
checklist.done: every candidate event is either an opened exception with a root cause, owner and date, or a written not-an-exception rationale.

checklist.step: Monitor for out-of-cycle statutory change during the year
actions: Subscribe the regulatory change feed to all 51 departments for the terms unfair trade practices, rebating, inducement, advertising and unfair discrimination.
Triage each hit within 5 business days into no-impact, appendix-only update, or procedure rewrite, and record the triage decision with the bulletin reference.
Open an out-of-cycle change task with a 60-day completion clock for anything above no-impact and assign it to the procedure owner.
Report open out-of-cycle tasks to the Head of Compliance in the monthly compliance pack.
checklist.done: every regulatory change hit is triaged within 5 business days and anything with impact has a 60-day task on the procedure owner.

checklist.step: Retain the procedure evidence for the exam look-back
actions: File the year's package - approved PDFs, superseded versions, 51 statute captures, appendices, legal clearance memo, training completion extract, exception log export - under Market Conduct / Model 880 / <yyyy>.
Apply the 7-year retention label so the record outlives the next market conduct examination look-back.
Confirm the repository index makes the package searchable by jurisdiction, procedure name and version number.
Run a restore test on one prior-year package to prove superseded versions are still retrievable.
checklist.done: the annual package is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, indexed by jurisdiction and proven retrievable by a restore test.

testing.step: Build the population of procedures, appendices and conduct exceptions
actions: Extract from the repository every published UTPA procedure version effective during the test year with its approval date, approver and next review date.
Extract all 51 appendix rows per procedure and the full conduct exception log for the year.
Reconcile the procedure count to the six controls registered in the GRC platform and resolve any procedure that exists in one place and not the other before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the GRC control register and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the procedure set to the Model 880 Section 4 sub-part list
actions: List the Section 4 sub-parts independently from the model text rather than from the company inventory.
Match each sub-part to a controlling instruction inside a published procedure, citing the procedure name and section number.
Record any sub-part with no controlling instruction as an automatic exception, including sub-parts covered only by a training slide.
testing.done: every Section 4 sub-part is traced to a named procedure section or listed as an uncovered exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the appendix sample
actions: Take 100% of the jurisdictions that amended their UTPA or issued a relevant bulletin during the year.
Add 15 further jurisdictions drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remaining states, minimum 25 jurisdictions in total.
Record the seed, population size and draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every jurisdiction that changed its law during the year.

testing.step: Re-read the statute for each sampled jurisdiction and re-perform the appendix call
actions: Open the department's current statute page for the sampled jurisdiction and read the UTPA chapter without first reading the appendix row.
Form your own conclusion on whether the state deviates from the Model 880 baseline on advertising, rebating and discrimination class list.
Compare to the appendix row; treat a right conclusion supported by a repealed or renumbered cite as an exception.
Save the statute page capture with its retrieval date into the workpaper as the support for your conclusion.
testing.done: each sampled jurisdiction has an independent conclusion, a dated statute capture and a documented agree/disagree against the appendix.

testing.step: Test the advertising file against pieces actually in market
actions: Pull 20 pieces that were live during the year from the campaign send log and the public website archive, weighted to digital and agent-produced material.
For each piece find the review record: approval date, reviewer, states of use, first and last date used.
Confirm the approval date pre-dates the first use date and that the states of use are all states where the piece was actually served.
Log any piece used before approval or outside its approved states as a prohibited-practice exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled live piece traces to an approval that pre-dates first use and covers the states it ran in.

testing.step: Test the inducement clearance register against real offers
actions: Select 15 offers of goods, services, gifts or fee waivers from marketing campaign records and producer expense claims during the year.
Trace each to a clearance register entry with a per-recipient value and a permitted-state list.
Re-apply the state grid: check the per-recipient value against that state's cap and the nexus test for value-added services.
Treat any offer made in a state where the grid says prohibited as a reportable breach requiring a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every sampled offer has a cleared register entry whose value and state list survive re-application of the grid.

testing.step: Verify the complaint record satisfies Section 4(10)
actions: Export the complaint register for the period since the date of the last market conduct examination.
Confirm the export carries total number, line of insurance classification, nature, disposition and time-to-process for every case with no nulls.
Re-compute time-to-process for 25 cases from the receipt and final-response timestamps and compare to the reported value.
Trace 10 department-forwarded complaints to the department acknowledgement and confirm the response met that state's stated deadline.
testing.done: the complaint register carries all five mandated fields with no nulls and the recomputed time-to-process agrees on every re-tested case.

testing.step: Recompute training coverage and the review-cycle dates
actions: Rebuild the assignment population independently from HRIS job codes and the appointed producer list and compare it to the population the LMS was given.
Compute completion rate as completions divided by the independently rebuilt population and compare to the 98% threshold.
Recompute each procedure's elapsed days from approval date to test date and flag any procedure past its 31 May next-review date.
Flag any producer who failed the assessment twice and remained appointed.
testing.done: completion is recomputed against an independently built population and every procedure's review date is tested against the annual cycle.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying jurisdiction, Model 880 sub-part, what was missed and the policyholder impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list and an owner at manager level or above, with a remediation date inside 60 days.
Open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any exception showing a prohibited practice reached a policyholder.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate by procedure and compare against the stated fail thresholds for approval currency, cite validity, training completion and exception ageing.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with evidence references behind each supporting statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted none of the six procedures, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open prohibited-practice breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Code tit. 27 ch. 12, ALDOI; supporting Arizona, California, Connecticut adoptions of NAIC Model 880), read together with the current-year NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for each participating line

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Property/casualty lines (private passenger auto, homeowners, lender-placed) due 30 April for the prior data year; life, annuity, long-term care, health and disability income lines due 30 June; participation is triggered by direct written premium in the state for the data year at the threshold stated in that line's data call (commonly USD 50,000)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Reporting calendar tasks at T-90 (data dictionary and participation list frozen), T-60 (first full extract), T-30 (validation clean), T-10 (attestation packet to the officer) against each of the 30 April and 30 June due dates

checklist.step: Load this data year's MCAS Data Call and Definitions and diff the blanks
actions: Download the current-year Data Call and Definitions and the blank templates for every line the company may report, from the NAIC MCAS page.
Diff this year's blank against last year's line by line and list added, removed and re-defined elements, including changed definitions of claim counts, lawsuit counts and days-to-payment.
List the changed interrogatories separately - they usually need a business answer, not a data extract.
Send the diff to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with the mapping work each change creates.
checklist.done: a written blank diff exists for every reportable line, split into data-element changes and interrogatory changes, and is accepted by the reporting owner.

checklist.step: Determine participation per state and line from direct written premium
actions: Extract direct written premium by state, line and writing company for the data year and tie it to the statutory annual statement state page for the same year.
Apply each line's participation threshold from the data call (commonly USD 50,000 direct written premium in the state for the data year) and mark each state/line in or out.
Cross-check the resulting list against the NAIC's published participating-states list for each line - a state can require reporting even where the company sits just under.
Record borderline states (within 10% of the threshold) on a watch list and report them to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for a report-anyway decision.
checklist.done: a participation matrix exists by state, line and writing company, tied to the annual statement state page, with borderline cases decided.

checklist.step: Freeze the source-to-blank data dictionary
actions: For every element on every reportable blank, record the source system, table and field, the filter logic, the date basis (transaction date vs effective date) and the owner who signed the definition.

Resolve elements that the source cannot produce cleanly - claims closed without payment, days to final payment, suits opened and closed - by writing an agreed derivation with the Claims Analyst rather than an estimate.
Have the Business Systems Analyst confirm the policy administration and claims platform field names still exist after this year's releases.
Version the dictionary and publish it as the single reference for the extract build.
checklist.done: every blank element has a named source field, filter logic, date basis and a signed definition in a versioned dictionary.

checklist.step: Build and run the MCAS extract
actions: Implement the extract from the frozen dictionary, one job per line, producing one output row per state and writing company in the NAIC blank column order.
Run the job for the full data year and produce a control report: record counts, premium totals, claim counts and policy counts by state.
Re-run the prior data year through the same code and compare to what was filed last year - a difference means either a code change or a restatement, and both must be explained.
Hand the output plus the control report to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and keep the job run id for the evidence pack.
checklist.done: the extract runs clean for every reportable line with a control report and an explained prior-year re-run comparison.

checklist.step: Reconcile MCAS totals to the financial and claims systems of record
actions: Tie MCAS direct written premium by state to the statutory annual statement state page for the same data year and explain every variance above 0.5%.
Tie claim counts and paid amounts to the claims platform period reports and to the general ledger paid-loss balance.
Tie policy counts in force at year end to the policy administration in-force report.
Document each variance with a cause (timing, cancellation handling, line mapping) and get the Controller to acknowledge the premium tie in writing.
checklist.done: premium, claim and policy totals tie to the annual statement, claims system and policy system with every variance above 0.5% explained in writing.

checklist.step: Draft the interrogatory and narrative responses
actions: Answer each line's interrogatories from current operating fact - use of third-party data in underwriting, replacement handling, suitability review, complaint handling arrangements - not from last year's text.
Where an answer changed from last year, note internally why it changed so the change is defensible if a state asks.
Have Regulatory Counsel review any interrogatory answer that describes a practice touching rebating, discrimination or advertising.
Lock the answers before upload and store the approved text with the evidence pack.
checklist.done: every interrogatory has a current, owner-approved answer, with counsel review on the conduct-sensitive ones.

checklist.step: Upload each blank into the NAIC MCAS application and clear validations
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS online application with the company's assigned user id, select the data year and the line, and choose the state.
Upload the line's completed template (or key the blank directly for small states) and run the validation.
Work every validation message to closure: hard errors must be fixed in the data, soft warnings must carry an explanatory comment in the comment field rather than being left silent.

Where a warning is genuinely correct behaviour - for example a high closed-without-payment ratio driven by a catastrophe - write the explanation in the comment field so the analyst reading the scorecard sees it.
Save each state/line in the application only after it validates clean or carries an explained warning.
checklist.done: every state/line blank is uploaded and shows either clean validation or a warning carrying a written explanation.

checklist.step: Review the ratios before submitting and pre-empt the outlier question
actions: Compute the ratios the states score - claims closed without payment ratio, median and mean days to final payment, suits opened per 1,000 claims, complaint counts, replacement and surrender ratios for life/annuity - by state and line.
Compare each to the company's own prior two data years and to the industry ratios published from prior MCAS cycles.
For every state/line ratio that moved materially or sits well outside the peer range, write a one-paragraph business explanation with the operational driver.
Hand the outlier pack to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager so the answer exists before a state asks.
checklist.done: a ratio pack exists with a written explanation for every material outlier, held ready for a department inquiry.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation for each submission
actions: Receive the attestation packet: the exact data to be submitted, the reconciliation summary, the outlier explanations and the list of open data caveats.
Challenge any caveat that says an element is estimated and require the derivation to be documented before signing.
Sign the attestation in the NAIC MCAS application for each line as an officer of the company.
Return unsigned any packet delivered later than T-10 days before the due date and record the delay as a process exception.
checklist.done: an officer attestation is recorded in the application for every line, backed by a reviewed packet with no unexplained estimates.

checklist.step: Submit every state and line and capture the confirmations
actions: Submit each state/line in the MCAS application before its due date - 30 April for the property/casualty lines, 30 June for the life, annuity, long-term care, health and disability income lines.
Screenshot or export the submission confirmation showing company, data year, line, state, submission timestamp and status Submitted.
Tick each row of the participation matrix off against a confirmation and chase any state showing In Progress at T-2 days.
File the confirmations, the submitted files and the validation reports in the compliance evidence repository under Market Conduct / MCAS / <data year>.
checklist.done: every row of the participation matrix has a dated submission confirmation filed before its due date.

checklist.step: Handle post-submission corrections and restatements
actions: Where an error is found after submission, quantify the affected elements and states before touching the application.
Request the NAIC MCAS help desk to reopen the affected state/line filing, restate the data and re-attest.
Notify the affected department in writing where the restatement changes a scored ratio, with the cause and the corrective action.
Log the restatement as an exception with root cause and a control change so the same element cannot break again.
checklist.done: each correction is quantified, re-submitted and re-attested, with department notification where a scored ratio moved.

checklist.step: Feed MCAS results back into conduct monitoring
actions: Load the submitted MCAS data into the conduct monitoring dashboard alongside complaint and internal quality metrics.
Set watch thresholds on the ratios that drive state market analysis scoring so deterioration is seen during the year, not at the next filing.
Open an improvement action for any ratio in the worst quartile against peers with an owner in the operating area that drives it.
Report the MCAS position to the Compliance Committee within 60 days of submission.
checklist.done: submitted MCAS data is loaded into monitoring with thresholds set and worst-quartile ratios owned by an operating area.

checklist.step: Update the reporting calendar and control record for the next cycle
actions: Roll the calendar forward with the 30 April and 30 June due dates and the T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10 milestones for the next data year.
Record the completed submission against the GRC control with links to the confirmations.
Carry forward any blank-diff mapping work and any unresolved data-quality item as a dated task on a named owner.
Book the participation-determination task for January so the matrix is built before the extract work starts.
checklist.done: next cycle's milestones, owners and carried-forward data issues are on the calendar and the control record shows this cycle complete.

checklist.step: Answer state MCAS follow-up inquiries within the stated window
actions: Log every department inquiry referencing MCAS data with the state, the ratio or element questioned and the stated response deadline.
Pull the submitted blank and the ratio pack explanation for that state/line and draft the response against the actual filed figures.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response conceding a reporting error before it is sent, and send through the department's stated channel.
Close the tracker item with the response, the send date and the department acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every MCAS inquiry is answered inside its deadline with the response, send date and acknowledgement on the tracker item.

checklist.step: Retain the MCAS evidence pack
actions: File per data year and line: participation matrix, data dictionary version, extract job id and control report, reconciliations, submitted files, validation reports, ratio pack, attestations and confirmations.
Apply the 7-year retention label so the pack survives into the next market conduct examination look-back.
Index the pack by state, line and data year so a single state's filing can be produced on its own.
Test retrieval of one prior-year state/line pack and record the test result.
checklist.done: the pack is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, indexed by state and line and proven retrievable.

testing.step: Rebuild the required-submission population independently
actions: Extract direct written premium by state, line and writing company for the data year straight from the warehouse without using the reporting team's participation matrix.
Apply each line's participation threshold from the published Data Call and Definitions to derive your own required state/line list.
Reconcile your list to the statutory annual statement state page and to the NAIC published participating-states list and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: an independently derived required-submission population exists, reconciled to the annual statement state page.

testing.step: Reconcile required submissions to confirmed submissions
actions: Match every row of the independent population to a submission confirmation in the NAIC MCAS application showing status Submitted.
Compare each submission timestamp to its due date - 30 April for the property/casualty lines, 30 June for the life and health lines.
List every unmatched state/line and every submission after the due date as an automatic exception with no judgement applied.
Also list any submission made for a state/line that the population says was not required, to catch mis-scoped filings.
testing.done: every required state/line is matched to a timely confirmation or recorded as a completeness or timeliness exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the data-accuracy sample
actions: Take 100% of the five largest states by direct written premium and every state carrying an unresolved validation warning.
Add 10 further state/line combinations drawn at random with a recorded seed, minimum 20 combinations in total.

Within each selected blank, list the elements to re-perform: written premium, policies in force, claims closed with and without payment, median days to final payment, suits opened, complaints received.
Record the seed, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of state/line blanks and named elements is documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled data elements from source
actions: Rebuild each sampled element directly from the policy administration and claims platforms using the frozen data dictionary definition, not the reporting team's extract.
Compare your figure to the submitted blank value and compute the variance percentage on each element.
Treat any variance above 0.5% as a data-accuracy exception and identify whether the cause is the definition, the filter or the source data.
Capture the source query and the run timestamp into the workpaper so the re-performance can be repeated.
testing.done: every sampled element is independently rebuilt with a computed variance and a cause assigned to each variance above 0.5%.

testing.step: Recompute the scored ratios from the submitted data
actions: Recompute claims closed without payment ratio, median days to final payment and suits opened per 1,000 claims from the submitted blank figures for each sampled state/line.
Compare to the ratio pack the compliance team produced and to the prior two data years.
Confirm every ratio flagged as an outlier carries a written business explanation, and that the explanation matches an operational fact you can verify.
Flag any outlier with no explanation as an exception because it is the ratio a state analyst will ask about first.
testing.done: the scored ratios recompute to the ratio pack and every outlier carries a verifiable written explanation.

testing.step: Test the attestation and its supporting packet
actions: Confirm an officer attestation exists in the MCAS application for every submitted line and that the signer is an officer of the writing company.
Compare the attestation date to the submission date and to the T-10 packet delivery milestone.
Read the packet caveats and confirm no element described as estimated was submitted without a documented derivation.
Treat an attestation signed without the reconciliation summary attached as a control failure regardless of data accuracy.
testing.done: each line has an officer attestation backed by a dated, complete packet with no undocumented estimates.

testing.step: Verify validation warnings were resolved rather than ignored
actions: Pull the validation report for each sampled state/line from the MCAS application.
Confirm no hard error remained open at submission and that each soft warning carries a comment in the application comment field.
Read the comment and confirm it states a cause rather than repeating the warning text.
Log warnings closed with an empty or circular comment as documentation exceptions.
testing.done: no sampled submission carries an open hard error or an unexplained soft warning.

testing.step: Test restatements and late submissions for notification
actions: List every reopened or restated state/line for the data year from the application history and the exception log.
For each, recompute whether the restatement moved a scored ratio and whether the affected department was notified in writing.
Check the exception record carries a root cause and a control change, not just a corrected number.
Treat a restatement that moved a scored ratio with no department notification as a reportable breach.
testing.done: every restatement is traced to a ratio-impact assessment and, where impacted, a written department notification.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with data year, state, line, element and the completeness, timeliness or accuracy category.
Assign a root cause (participation missed, dictionary wrong, source field changed, calendar slipped) and an owner in Regulatory Reporting or the source operating area.
Set remediation dates that land before the next cycle's T-90 dictionary freeze so fixes are in place before the next extract.
Carry open exceptions into the next cycle's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, a remediation date before the next T-90 freeze and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute completeness (required vs submitted), timeliness (submitted vs due date) and accuracy (elements within 0.5%) rates for the cycle.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-tolerance completeness and timeliness thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer, who built no extract and keyed no blank, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missed or late submissions to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under Market Conduct / MCAS / <data year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completeness, timeliness and accuracy rates with a conclusion and a committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Fix the conduct metric definitions and their owners for the year
actions: List the monitored metrics with an exact definition: complaints per 1,000 policies in force, department-forwarded complaint share, mean and median days to complaint closure, claims closed without payment ratio, median days to final claim payment, suits opened per 1,000 claims, decline and non-renewal rate, life replacement and surrender ratio, advertising disapproval rate, producer conduct allegations per 100 appointed producers.
Match each definition to the equivalent MCAS element wording so the internal metric and the filed ratio move together.

Name an operating owner for each metric - Complaints Manager, Claims Director / Manager, Underwriting Director / Manager, Head of Distribution, Marketing Compliance Analyst - and get each to accept the definition in writing.
Publish the definitions sheet as the reference the dashboard is built from.
checklist.done: every metric has an exact definition aligned to MCAS wording and a written acceptance from a named operating owner.

checklist.step: Set the benchmark and trigger thresholds from external data
actions: Pull the company complaint index and peer indices from the NAIC Consumer Information Source for the prior year, by state and line.
Pull the published industry MCAS ratios for the prior data year for each reported line to set the peer distribution for claims and policyholder-service metrics.

Set two levels per metric per state: a watch level (worse than the 75th percentile of peers or a 25% deterioration on rolling four quarters) and a trigger level (worse than the 90th percentile or a 50% deterioration).
Record the source and date of every benchmark figure next to the threshold so the number can be defended, and have the Head of Compliance approve the threshold set.
checklist.done: each metric carries a sourced, dated watch and trigger threshold by state, approved by the Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly data extracts behind the metrics
actions: Build one extract per metric family: complaints from the case tool, claim events from the claims platform, decisions from the policy administration platform, appointments and allegations from the producer management system.
Key every extract by state, line, writing company and quarter, and carry the source record id so any metric can be drilled back to individual cases.

Run reasonableness controls - complaint count against the case tool's own dashboard, policies in force against the in-force report, claim counts against the claims period report - and stop the refresh on any variance above 1%.
Schedule the extracts to run on the third working day after quarter end and record the run id for the evidence pack.
checklist.done: each metric family has a keyed, drillable quarterly extract that passes its reasonableness control before publication.

checklist.step: Refresh the conduct monitoring dashboard
actions: Publish the quarter's metrics with a rolling eight-quarter trend, state and line filters and the watch/trigger bands drawn on each chart.
Add a drill-through from any metric point to the underlying record list so a reviewer can open the actual complaints or claims behind a number.
Show the benchmark line and its source label on each chart so the peer comparison is visible without leaving the page.
Notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager when the refresh completes and freeze a dated snapshot of the pack pages.
checklist.done: the dashboard shows the quarter with trend, bands, benchmark labels and record-level drill-through, and a dated snapshot is frozen.

checklist.step: Run the complaint index and complaint-driver review
actions: Compare the internal complaints-per-1,000-policies figure by state to the NAIC Consumer Information Source complaint index for the company.
Break the quarter's complaints by reason code (underwriting, marketing and sales, policyholder service, claim handling) and by disposition code, and rank the top five drivers per state.
Pull the ten longest-running open complaints and confirm each has an owner and a next action dated inside the state's response window.
Hand the driver ranking to the operating owner of each driver with a response due before the pack date.
checklist.done: the complaint index comparison, top-five driver ranking per state and long-runner review are complete with owner responses requested.

checklist.step: Run the claims conduct metric review
actions: Read the claims closed without payment ratio, median days to final payment and suits opened per 1,000 claims by state and line against the MCAS peer distribution.
For any state above its trigger level, pull 20 closed-without-payment files and confirm each carries a coverage rationale and a written denial explanation to the insured.
Check the days-to-payment tail for files paid beyond the state's prompt-payment expectation and list the causes.
Send the file review findings to the Claims Director / Manager with a corrective action request where a pattern shows.
checklist.done: every triggered claims metric has a 20-file review with documented causes and a corrective action request to Claims.

checklist.step: Run the underwriting and rating fairness review
actions: Compute decline, non-renewal and tier-assignment rates by state, product and distribution channel for the quarter.
Look for unexplained dispersion between geographies within a state and hand any material dispersion to the Pricing Actuary for an explanation grounded in loss experience.
Pull 15 declines in the highest-dispersion state and confirm each records a permitted underwriting reason and an insured notification consistent with the state's requirements.
Escalate to Market Conduct Compliance any pattern that cannot be explained by risk characteristics, because that is the unfair discrimination exposure.
checklist.done: dispersion is measured, 15 declines are file-reviewed in the worst state, and unexplained patterns are escalated.

checklist.step: Run the sales, advertising and rebating conduct review
actions: Report advertising pieces submitted, approved, disapproved and used-without-approval for the quarter, with the disapproval reasons grouped.
Report inducement clearance requests, approvals and refusals, and any offer found in market without clearance.
Report life and annuity replacement and surrender ratios by producer and flag producers above the trigger for a Producer Compliance Manager file review.
Attach the quarter's counts to the pack with the top three recurring disapproval reasons named, because those are the training gaps.
checklist.done: advertising, inducement and replacement counts are reported with recurring disapproval reasons named and producer reviews raised.

checklist.step: Analyse every threshold breach to a driver
actions: List every metric-state-line series above its watch or trigger level for the quarter.
For each, decompose the movement into volume, mix, process and data-quality components rather than reporting the movement alone.
Pull the underlying records through the dashboard drill-through and read enough of them to name the operational driver.
Write a one-page breach note per trigger breach with driver, affected policyholder or claimant count, and the proposed corrective action.
checklist.done: every watch and trigger breach has a decomposed driver analysis and, for triggers, a one-page breach note with an impact count.

checklist.step: Open and assign conduct issues for trigger breaches
actions: Open one conduct issue per trigger breach carrying state, line, metric, quarter, driver and impacted count.
Assign the operating owner named in the definitions sheet, not a compliance analyst, and agree a corrective action with a completion date inside the next quarter.
Set the closure rule on the issue: two consecutive quarters back inside the watch level before it can close.
Link the issue to the relevant Model 880 sub-part where the metric evidences a prohibited-practice exposure.
checklist.done: every trigger breach has an owned issue with a dated corrective action and a two-clean-quarters closure rule.

checklist.step: Assemble and issue the quarterly conduct pack
actions: Build the pack: metric scorecard by state and line, benchmark comparison, movement commentary, breach notes, open issue ageing and last quarter's actions with status.
State the data cut date and the source extract run ids on the cover so the numbers are reproducible.
Circulate to the operating owners for factual challenge with a 3-working-day window and record every challenge and its resolution.
Issue the final pack to the Compliance Committee by working day 25 after quarter end.
checklist.done: a challenged, source-referenced pack is issued to the Compliance Committee by working day 25.

checklist.step: Take the pack through the Compliance Committee and record decisions
actions: Present the trigger breaches, the impacted policyholder counts and the proposed corrective actions.
Obtain a decision on each breach: accept the corrective action, demand a deeper review, or escalate to the board risk committee where multi-state.
Have the Corporate Secretary minute each decision with the owner and date so the minute itself is exam evidence.
Feed any decision that changes a procedure into the UTPA procedure out-of-cycle review task.
checklist.done: every trigger breach carries a minuted committee decision with an owner and date.

checklist.step: Track corrective actions to closure across quarters
actions: Age every open conduct issue at each refresh and report anything past its due date to the Head of Compliance.
Recheck the metric for each open issue against its watch level and record the quarter-by-quarter position on the issue.
Close an issue only after two consecutive quarters inside the watch level, with the Head of Compliance sign-off recorded on the issue.
Reopen rather than raise a new issue where a closed metric breaches again within four quarters, so the history stays intact.
checklist.done: issue ageing is reported each quarter and closures occur only after two clean quarters with recorded sign-off.

checklist.step: Re-baseline thresholds when new benchmark data publishes
actions: When the new NAIC complaint index year and the new industry MCAS ratios publish, recompute the peer percentiles per metric and state.
Compare the new watch and trigger levels to the current ones and list every threshold that moves by more than 10%.
Present the proposed re-baseline to the Head of Compliance with the reason for each move - a loosened threshold needs an explicit justification, not a silent update.
Version the threshold sheet and keep the superseded version so prior quarters remain assessable against the thresholds in force at the time.
checklist.done: thresholds are recomputed against the new benchmark year, material moves are justified and approved, and the prior version is retained.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring evidence
actions: File each quarter's pack, dashboard snapshot, extract run ids, breach notes, issue export and committee minute under Market Conduct / Monitoring / <year> Q<n>.
Apply the 7-year retention label so four years of trend remain available to the next examination.
Index by state, metric and quarter so a single state's trend can be produced on request.
Test retrieval of a prior-year quarter and record the result.
checklist.done: each quarter's evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, indexed by state and metric and proven retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of quarters, metrics and breaches
actions: List the quarterly packs issued for the period under test with their issue dates and data cut dates.
Extract every metric-state-line series from the frozen dashboard snapshots and flag those above watch and trigger levels.
Reconcile the flagged series count to the conduct issues opened in the GRC platform for the same quarters and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population of packs, series and breaches reconciles to the GRC issue register and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Test pack completeness and timeliness against the calendar
actions: Confirm a pack exists for every quarter in the period with no gaps.
Recompute working day 25 from each quarter end and compare to the pack issue date recorded in the distribution record.
Confirm each pack states its data cut date and the extract run ids on the cover.
Record any missing pack, late issue or missing source reference as an exception.
testing.done: every quarter has a pack issued by working day 25 carrying its data cut date and run ids, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the metric sample
actions: Take 100% of metric-state-line series that breached a trigger during the period.
Add 12 further series drawn at random with a recorded seed across complaints, claims, underwriting and sales metric families.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Note for each selected series which quarter's figure will be re-performed.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering every trigger breach plus 12 random series is documented.

testing.step: Recompute each sampled metric from source records
actions: Rebuild each sampled metric from the source systems using the published definition, without reusing the monitoring extract.
Compare to the reported figure and compute the variance percentage.
Treat any variance above 2% as an exception and identify whether the cause is the definition, the filter, the date basis or a source data change.
Save the query, the run timestamp and the result into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled metric is independently recomputed with a variance and a named cause for each variance above 2%.

testing.step: Re-test the benchmark and threshold derivation
actions: Take the benchmark figure cited for each sampled metric and trace it to the NAIC Consumer Information Source complaint index or the published industry MCAS ratio it claims to come from.
Recompute the watch and trigger levels from the stated percentile or deterioration rule.
Confirm the threshold applied in the quarter is the version that was in force at the time, not a later re-baseline.
Flag any threshold loosened without a documented Head of Compliance justification.
testing.done: each sampled threshold traces to a dated external benchmark and recomputes to the stated rule using the version in force.

testing.step: Trace trigger breaches to opened issues and driver analysis
actions: For every trigger breach in the population, find the conduct issue and confirm it was opened in the same quarter the breach was reported.
Read the breach note and confirm it names an operational driver and an impacted policyholder or claimant count rather than restating the movement.
Confirm the assigned owner sits in the operating area, not in Compliance, and that a corrective action carries a date inside the following quarter.
Log any breach with no issue, no driver or a compliance-only owner as an exception.
testing.done: every trigger breach has a same-quarter issue with an operational owner, a named driver and a dated corrective action.

testing.step: Re-perform the underlying file reviews on a sub-sample
actions: Take 10 of the files the claims metric review examined and read them independently for a coverage rationale and a written denial explanation to the insured.
Take 10 declines from the underwriting fairness review and confirm a permitted underwriting reason and the insured notification are on file.
Compare your conclusions to the reviewer's findings and note any file the reviewer passed that you would fail.
Capture the file identifiers and screenshots into the workpaper.
testing.done: 20 files are independently re-read with conclusions compared to the original reviewer and differences documented.

testing.step: Test closure discipline and issue ageing
actions: List every conduct issue closed in the period and read the metric history behind each closure.
Recompute whether two consecutive quarters sat inside the watch level before closure and check the Head of Compliance sign-off is recorded on the issue.
Check whether any metric closed in the period breached again within four quarters and whether the original issue was reopened rather than replaced.
Log premature closures and replacement-instead-of-reopen cases as exceptions.
testing.done: every closure is supported by two clean quarters and a recorded sign-off, with repeat breaches traced to reopened issues.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the quarter, metric, state and the completeness, accuracy, escalation or closure category.
Assign a root cause (definition drift, extract error, threshold not applied, escalation missed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarter's data cut so the next pack is produced on the fixed basis.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, a remediation date before the next data cut and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the metric accuracy rate, the pack timeliness rate and the breach escalation rate for the period.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the stated thresholds, naming any state where monitoring failed to surface a real conduct issue.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no monitored metric and produced no pack, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under Market Conduct / Monitoring.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with accuracy, timeliness and escalation rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Map the readiness file index to the handbook examination standards
actions: Create an index section per NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standard area: Operations and Management, Complaint Handling, Marketing and Sales, Producer Licensing, Policyholder Service, Underwriting and Rating, and Claims.
Under each section list the record sets an examiner will call for, with the source system, the owner and the refresh cadence.
Extend the index by writing company and by jurisdiction so a single-state exam can be scoped without rebuilding it.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the index as the definition of exam-ready.
checklist.done: an approved index exists with at least one owned, sourced record set under every handbook standard area, split by company and jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Specify and build the standing exam extracts
actions: Write an extract specification per record set - policies issued, declines and non-renewals, cancellations, claims opened/closed/denied, complaints, producer appointments and terminations, commission payments, advertising pieces - each keyed by state, writing company, line and period.
Include on every extract the record identifier the source system uses so an examiner's sample can be traced back to a file in one hop.
Match field names and definitions to the handbook's usual request wording so the extract needs no translation for the examiner.
Schedule monthly refreshes and store each run with its run id, row counts and the period covered.
checklist.done: every record set has a keyed, identifier-carrying standing extract refreshing monthly with run ids retained.

checklist.step: Reconcile the standing extracts to the systems of record quarterly
actions: Tie policy and premium extracts to the policy administration in-force and written premium reports by state.
Tie claim extracts to the claims platform period reports and the general ledger paid-loss balance.
Tie complaint extracts to the case tool register and to the count reported in MCAS for the same period.
Explain every variance above 1% in writing and open a readiness gap where the variance cannot be explained inside the quarter.
checklist.done: each standing extract ties to its system of record with every variance above 1% explained or logged as a readiness gap.

checklist.step: Keep the complaint record in the Section 4(10) form continuously
actions: Run a monthly register export covering the period since the date of the last market conduct examination, with total number, line classification, nature, disposition and time to process.
Reject the export if any case is missing a nature or disposition code and drive the gaps back to the handling team the same month.
Separate department-forwarded complaints from direct complaints on the export because examiners reconcile the department set against their own records first.
Store each monthly export in the readiness file so the register can be produced as at any month end.
checklist.done: a complete, code-populated complaint register export exists for every month since the last examination, split by complaint source.

checklist.step: Keep the advertising file exam-ready
actions: Maintain one advertising file entry per piece with piece id, media, creator, approving reviewer and date, states of use, and first and last date used.
Attach the actual creative - print PDF, email render, landing page capture, social post capture - because a description is not the piece.
Reconcile the file monthly against the campaign send log and the website publication log to catch pieces that went live outside the queue.
Log any piece found in market with no file entry as a readiness gap and as a conduct exception.
checklist.done: every piece used in the period has a file entry with the creative attached, reconciled monthly against send and publication logs.

checklist.step: Keep producer licensing and appointment records exam-ready
actions: Reconcile the internal appointed-producer list to NIPR appointment records by state and writing company each month and clear mismatches.
Hold for each producer the licence number, lines of authority, appointment effective date, and where terminated the termination date and reason code as reported to the state.
Confirm no commission was paid to a producer not appointed and licensed in the state at the transaction date by matching the commission extract to the appointment record.
Log unappointed-producer commission payments to the Head of Compliance immediately - examiners test this in every exam.
checklist.done: the appointed-producer list reconciles to NIPR monthly and no commission payment sits against an unappointed producer.

checklist.step: Keep the underwriting, rating and forms record set current
actions: Maintain the register of forms and rate/rule manuals in force by state with edition dates, SERFF tracking numbers and the effective date each was implemented in the rating engine.
Hold the underwriting guidelines version in force for each period so a file reviewed by an examiner is judged against the rules that applied at the time.
Keep the decline, cancellation and non-renewal extracts with the reason code and the notice sent to the insured.
Confirm quarterly that the rating engine configuration effective dates match the filed approval dates and escalate any mismatch.
checklist.done: forms, manuals, guidelines versions and decision notices are held per state and period, with rating effective dates matching filed approvals.

checklist.step: Keep the claims record set and claim file assembly ready
actions: Maintain the claims extract with opened, closed-with-payment, closed-without-payment and reopened populations by state, line and period.
Confirm the claim file assembly job can produce a complete file - notes, correspondence, payments, denial letter, reserve history - as a single indexed PDF within one working day of request.
Sample five files a month and check the assembled output actually contains the denial explanation and the payment detail an examiner will look for.
Log any file the assembly cannot produce completely as a readiness gap against the claims system owner.
checklist.done: claims populations are extractable and the file-assembly job is proven monthly to produce complete indexed files within one working day.

checklist.step: Hold the governance evidence an Operations and Management review asks for
actions: File the current approved UTPA procedure set, the compliance charter, the committee terms of reference and the last four Compliance Committee minutes.
File the training rosters and completion evidence for conduct courses and the outsourcing and third-party administrator agreements with their oversight reports.
File the antifraud plan, the disaster recovery summary and the record retention schedule, since examiners request them in the Operations and Management standard.
Refresh each item on its own cadence and mark the index row with the as-at date.
checklist.done: every Operations and Management evidence item is filed with a current as-at date on the index row.

checklist.step: Run a mock data request twice a year
actions: Draft a mock call letter and initial data request modelled on a real state request for a chosen line and state, with a 10-working-day clock.
Issue it to the record owners without warning and time each response line from issue to delivery.
Score each line on completeness, format and traceability - does the extract carry identifiers that reach an actual file.
Write the findings into readiness gaps with owners and dates, and re-run the failed lines within 60 days.
checklist.done: a timed mock request has been run with per-line scores and every failed line has a dated readiness gap and a re-run.

checklist.step: Maintain the exam response protocol and the coordinator bench
actions: Name the exam coordinator and a deputy and record that all examiner contact routes through them, with business areas answering only through the coordinator.

Write the response workflow: log the request line, assign the owner, quality-check the output, obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance where privilege or an admission is involved, deliver through the examiner's stated secure channel, record the delivery.
Set the interview protocol - who may be interviewed, who attends with them, how commitments made in interviews are captured.
Rehearse the protocol with the record owners annually so the first exam of the year is not the rehearsal.
checklist.done: a named coordinator and deputy, a documented request workflow with counsel clearance points and an annual rehearsal record all exist.

checklist.step: Stand the file up on receipt of an actual call letter
actions: Log the call letter with state, examiner-in-charge, exam scope, period under review, lines and companies, and the response due date stated in the letter.
Explode the initial data request into one tracker task per line, assign the record owner and date each task at least 3 working days before the examiner's due date.
Freeze the standing extracts for the exam period so the figures given to the examiner cannot move underneath the exam.
Open the exam workspace and give the examiner-in-charge a single named contact and delivery channel.
checklist.done: the call letter is logged, every request line is an owned dated task, and the exam-period extracts are frozen.

checklist.step: Quality-check and deliver each response package
actions: Check each package answers the line as asked - right period, right companies, right states - and that record counts tie to the frozen extract.
Check identifiers are present so the examiner can pull any file from the list, and that personally identifiable data is handled per the examiner's stated transfer method.
Obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance on any package touching privileged material or conceding a deficiency.
Deliver through the examiner's channel, record the delivery date against the tracker task and keep a copy of exactly what was sent.
checklist.done: every package is count-tied, identifier-complete, counsel-cleared where required, delivered on time and archived as sent.

checklist.step: Close readiness gaps between exams
actions: Age all open readiness gaps monthly and report anything past due to the Head of Compliance.
Group recurring gaps by cause - source system cannot produce, ownership unclear, cadence not run - and fix the cause rather than the instance.
Require the Head of Compliance sign-off to close any gap that arose from a mock request failure.
Feed structural gaps into the annual readiness procedure review.
checklist.done: readiness gaps are aged monthly, closed with sign-off where they came from a mock failure, and recurring causes are fixed structurally.

checklist.step: Retain the readiness and exam evidence
actions: File the index, standing extract runs, reconciliations, mock request results, call letters, delivered packages and delivery records under Market Conduct / Exam Readiness by year and jurisdiction.
Retain the complaint record from the date of the last market conduct examination as Model 880 Section 4(10) requires and everything else for 7 years.
Index by jurisdiction, handbook standard and exam so a prior exam's full delivery set can be reproduced.
Test retrieval of one prior exam delivery set and record the result.
checklist.done: readiness and exam evidence is filed, retained to the Section 4(10) and 7-year rules, indexed by standard and proven retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of readiness records and exam responses
actions: Extract the readiness file index with every record set, owner, source and refresh cadence, split by writing company and jurisdiction.
Extract the standing extract run history for the period and every call letter, data request line and delivery record.
Reconcile the index rows to the record sets that actually exist in the repository and resolve any index row with no underlying record before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles index rows to actual record sets and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Test index coverage against the handbook standards
actions: List the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standard areas independently from the handbook rather than from the company index.
Map each standard area to at least one maintained record set with a named owner and a current as-at date.
Record any standard area with no record set, or with a record set whose as-at date is older than its stated cadence, as an automatic exception.
Repeat the coverage check for the three jurisdictions with the largest written premium.
testing.done: every handbook standard area maps to a current owned record set in the three largest jurisdictions, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the record-set sample
actions: Take 100% of record sets that failed a mock request line or carry an open readiness gap.
Add 12 record sets drawn at random with a recorded seed across the complaint, advertising, producer, underwriting and claims families.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the sample can be re-drawn.
For each selected record set note the period to be re-performed.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering every failed or gapped record set plus 12 random sets is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the extract-to-source reconciliation on the sample
actions: Rebuild the record counts for each sampled set straight from the source system for the stated period.
Compare to the standing extract counts and compute the variance percentage.
Treat any variance above 1% without a written explanation as an exception and identify whether the cause is period basis, state mapping or a missed transaction type.
Capture the source query and run timestamp into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled extract is independently recounted with a variance and a named cause for any variance above 1%.

testing.step: Trace sampled extract rows through to real files
actions: Pick 15 rows across the sampled extracts and use the carried identifier to open the underlying claim, policy, complaint or advertising record.
Confirm the record exists, matches the extract row on state, company, date and disposition, and can be produced as a complete indexed file.
Time the production of five claim files end to end against the one-working-day readiness standard.
Log any identifier that does not resolve to a producible record as an exception - an extract an examiner cannot follow is not evidence.
testing.done: every traced identifier resolves to a matching producible record and claim file production is timed against the one-day standard.

testing.step: Re-test the complaint record against Section 4(10)
actions: Export the complaint register covering the period since the date of the last market conduct examination.
Confirm total number, line classification, nature, disposition and time to process are populated on every case with no nulls.
Reconcile the department-forwarded subset to the departments' own correspondence log held by Consumer Affairs.
Treat any month with a missing export or any case with a blank code as an exception against the model requirement itself.
testing.done: the register is complete for the full period since the last exam with no blank mandated fields and a reconciled department subset.

testing.step: Re-test producer appointment and commission integrity
actions: Take 25 commission payments from the period and look up the paying state and transaction date.
Check NIPR for the producer's licence and appointment status in that state on that date.
Confirm terminated producers show a termination reason reported to the state within its required window.
Treat any commission paid to an unlicensed or unappointed producer as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: all 25 sampled commissions trace to a licensed and appointed producer on the transaction date, or a breach is reported.

testing.step: Recompute exam response timeliness
actions: List every data-request line issued by an examiner or by the mock request during the period with its due date and delivery date.
Recompute elapsed days for each line and compare to the due date stated in the call letter or mock letter.
Confirm each delivered package was counsel-cleared where it touched privilege or conceded a deficiency.
Log every line delivered after its due date, and every package delivered without a required clearance, as an exception.
testing.done: response timeliness is recomputed line by line and every late or unclear-cleared delivery is logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the handbook standard, jurisdiction, record set and the coverage, accuracy, traceability or timeliness category.
Assign a root cause (cadence not run, source cannot produce, ownership vacant, identifier missing) and an owner in the record-owning area.
Set a remediation date inside 60 days, shorter where an exam is open or expected.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test and into the next mock request as a mandatory line.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, a remediation date inside 60 days and a mock-request retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute coverage (standards with a current record set), accuracy (extracts within 1%), traceability (identifiers resolving to files) and timeliness rates.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - naming any handbook standard the company could not evidence today.
Have the independent reviewer, who maintains no readiness record and prepared no exam package, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under Market Conduct / Exam Readiness.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage, accuracy, traceability and timeliness rates with a conclusion and a committee reporting date.

Code tit. 27 ch. 12, ALDOI; supporting Arizona, California, Connecticut adoptions of NAIC Model 880), and each finding is re-read against the current text before a remediation is designed

In-scope systems.value: One remediation record per finding with milestones and evidence links; restitution executed through the claims platform and billing system, procedure changes landing in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Finding Remediation Procedure - draft report review and rebuttal, finding intake and severity rating, root cause analysis, corrective action plan with owners and dates, restitution calculation and payment, evidence pack assembly, regulator status reporting and closure verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel clearance on the rebuttal and consent-order sections; reviewed annually and after every closed exam using that exam's lessons

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Draft report written response due inside the window the department states in its transmittal (commonly 30 days from receipt); corrective action and restitution dates come from the adopted final report, consent order or regulatory settlement agreement and are tracked to the day, with status reports at the cadence the order requires
