checklist.step: Review the draft exam report and answer inside the department's window
actions: Log the draft report with the state, examiner-in-charge, exam period, and the written response deadline stated in the transmittal letter (commonly 30 days from receipt) and work back the internal drafting dates.
Break the report into individual findings and criticisms, one row each, with the standard examined, the sample tested, the error rate cited and the statute the examiner relied on.
Send each finding to the record owner for a factual check against the underlying files and collect written responses within 10 days.
Assemble the company response: accept, accept with clarification, or rebut with evidence attached, and never leave a finding unanswered.
checklist.done: every draft finding has a factual check and a stated position, and the response is ready ahead of the department's deadline.

checklist.step: Clear rebuttals with counsel and submit the response
actions: Read each rebuttal against the cited statute as it read during the exam period and drop any rebuttal that cannot be supported on the record.
Check the response concedes no more than the facts require and that any admission of a prohibited practice is deliberate and approved.
Approve the final response in writing and record the approval date.
Submit through the examiner's stated channel before the deadline and archive the submission confirmation with the exam file.
checklist.done: the response is counsel-approved, submitted before the deadline and archived with a submission confirmation.

checklist.step: Intake the adopted findings into a remediation register
actions: Open one register record per finding in the adopted final report, consent order or regulatory settlement agreement, carrying state, exam period, handbook standard, statute cited, examiner error rate and any monetary penalty.
Copy the committed remediation date and the required status-reporting cadence verbatim from the order - never a paraphrase and never an internal estimate.
Rate severity from policyholder impact and repeat status, and mark any finding that repeats a prior exam finding as Repeat.
Assign an executive owner in the operating area and a compliance lead to each record.
checklist.done: every adopted finding is a register record carrying the verbatim committed date, cadence, severity, repeat flag and two named owners.

checklist.step: Run a root cause analysis per finding
actions: Walk the process the finding sits in with the operating owner and map where the control that should have caught it sits.
Determine whether the cause is procedure, system configuration, training, capacity or deliberate practice, and evidence the conclusion with data rather than opinion.
Test whether the same cause exists in other states or lines that were not examined and record the wider exposure.
Write the cause and the wider exposure into the register record before any corrective action is designed.
checklist.done: each finding carries an evidenced root cause and a written assessment of the same exposure in unexamined states and lines.

checklist.step: Design the corrective action plan with dated milestones
actions: For each finding write the corrective actions that address the root cause - procedure change, system configuration change, control addition, retraining, or a staffing change - with an owner per action.
Date every action so the last one completes at least 30 days before the regulator-committed date, leaving room for evidence assembly.
Extend each action to the wider exposure identified in root cause, so the fix is not limited to the examined state.
Have the executive owner accept the plan in writing and load every milestone into the tracker with T-30/T-14/T-3 reminders.
checklist.done: each finding has an owner-accepted plan whose last milestone lands 30 days before the committed date, covering the wider exposure.

checklist.step: Build the restitution population where consumers were harmed
actions: Define the affected population from the finding's own terms - state, line, transaction type and the full period the order specifies, which is usually wider than the examiner's sample.
Extract every affected policy or claim with the identifier, the amount involved and the transaction date.
Reconcile the population count and value to the policy administration and claims systems and to the general ledger before any payment is calculated.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel agree the population definition in writing before proceeding.
checklist.done: the affected population is extracted for the full ordered period, reconciled to source and signed off on its definition.

checklist.step: Calculate restitution amounts including interest
actions: Compute the underpayment or overcharge per record as the difference between what was paid or charged and what should have been under the correct rate, form or claim handling.
Apply the interest rate and accrual basis the order or the state statute requires, from the original transaction date to the planned payment date.
Produce control totals by state and line and have the Controller agree them to a funding request in the general ledger.
Get the calculation methodology reviewed by a second preparer who did not build it and record the review.
checklist.done: per-record restitution with statutory interest is calculated, second-reviewed and tied to an agreed funding total.

checklist.step: Execute restitution payments and track delivery
actions: Issue payments through the claims or billing payment run with a distinct payment reason code so the restitution set can be identified later.
Send the explanatory letter the order requires with each payment, in the wording counsel cleared, and record the mailing date.
Track returned mail and uncashed payments, run address searches, and escalate the unreachable remainder to Regulatory Counsel for the state's unclaimed property route.
Reconcile payments issued to the calculated population weekly until every record is paid, escheated or documented as unreachable.
checklist.done: every record in the restitution population is paid, escheated or documented as unreachable, reconciled to the calculated total.

checklist.step: Change the procedure and the system so the finding cannot recur
actions: Update the affected UTPA procedure section, version it, obtain Head of Compliance approval and publish with the effective date.
Raise the system change through the normal change process with the finding reference on the change record, and confirm the configuration is live in every affected state.
Add or strengthen the control in the GRC platform with an owner, a frequency and a test method so the fix is monitored, not assumed.
Record the procedure version, change record number and control id against the finding in the register.
checklist.done: the finding register links to a published procedure version, a live change record and a monitored control.

checklist.step: Retrain the affected population and evidence it
actions: Build the retraining population from the roles that performed the failed activity, plus their supervisors.
Deliver targeted content built on the actual finding - the examiner's example, the correct handling, the control that now applies - not a generic conduct refresher.
Set a completion window inside the corrective action milestone and chase non-completion through the line manager.
Attach the completion extract to the finding record as closure evidence.
checklist.done: the targeted retraining is completed inside the milestone by the affected population with an extract attached to the finding.

checklist.step: Prove the corrective action is operating before claiming closure
actions: Wait at least one full operating cycle after the change, then sample 25 transactions processed after the effective date in the affected state and line.
Test each against the corrected requirement and compute the post-change error rate.
Compare it to the examiner's cited error rate and require it to sit inside the tolerance the order states, or below 5% where the order is silent.
Where the error rate has not moved, reopen the corrective action rather than closing the finding.
checklist.done: a post-change sample of 25 transactions demonstrates the error rate inside tolerance, or the corrective action is reopened.

checklist.step: Report status to the department at the ordered cadence
actions: Produce the status report in the format and at the cadence the consent order or final report requires, covering each finding's progress, restitution paid to date and remaining milestones.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the report where it describes scope of harm or a missed milestone.
Send through the department's stated channel before the due date and record the send date and acknowledgement.
Notify the department in advance, in writing, of any milestone that will be missed - never let the department discover a slip from the report.
checklist.done: every ordered status report is counsel-cleared, sent before its due date and acknowledged, with any slip notified in advance.

checklist.step: Assemble the closure package per finding
actions: Compile per finding: the finding text, root cause, corrective actions with completion evidence, procedure version, change record, control id, retraining extract, restitution reconciliation and the post-change sample result.
Index the package so any single item can be produced on its own at a re-exam.
Route to the Head of Compliance for sign-off and record the sign-off date on the register record.
Submit the package to the department where the order requires proof of completion, and file the department's closure letter against the finding.
checklist.done: each finding has a signed, indexed closure package and, where required, a department closure letter on file.

checklist.step: Escalate slipping and repeat findings
actions: Review the weekly overdue report and take personal ownership of any finding whose milestone has slipped twice.
Escalate to the board risk committee any finding flagged Repeat, any missed regulator-committed date and any restitution population found to be understated after payment started.
Decide and record whether a self-notification to the department is required and have Regulatory Counsel draft it.
Record the escalation, the decision and the revised date on the register record - a date may move only with a documented decision.
checklist.done: every twice-slipped, repeat or missed-commitment finding has a recorded escalation, decision and revised date.

checklist.step: Retain the remediation evidence and carry it to the next exam
actions: File per state and exam year: draft and final reports, company response, consent order, register export, closure packages, restitution payment files and the department closure letter.
Apply a 7-year-from-closure retention label so the set is available as prior-finding evidence at the next examination.
Add the closed findings to the exam readiness file so the next examiner's prior-findings request is answerable immediately.
Test retrieval of one closed finding's full package and record the result.
checklist.done: the remediation set is filed, retained 7 years from closure, loaded into the readiness file and proven retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of findings and commitments
actions: Extract every finding open or closed during the period from the remediation register with state, exam year, severity, repeat flag, committed date and status.
Rebuild the finding list independently by reading the adopted final reports and consent orders themselves rather than the register.
Reconcile the two lists and treat any finding present in a report but absent from the register as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the register reconciles finding-for-finding to the adopted reports and orders, with omissions logged.

testing.step: Recompute committed dates and milestone performance
actions: Read the committed remediation date and status-reporting cadence straight from each order and compare to what the register records.
Recompute elapsed days from adoption date to actual completion date for each finding and compare to the committed date.
Recompute each status report's due date from the ordered cadence and compare to the send date recorded.
Log every date the register paraphrased, every completion after the committed date and every late status report as an exception.
testing.done: every committed date is verified against the order text and every completion and status report is recomputed against it.

testing.step: Draw and document the finding sample
actions: Take 100% of findings closed in the period, all findings flagged Repeat and all findings carrying restitution.
Add 5 open findings drawn at random with a recorded seed to test in-flight discipline.
Record the seed, population size and draw date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note for each sampled finding which corrective action and which population will be re-performed.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all closed, repeat and restitution findings plus 5 open ones is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the restitution population build
actions: Rebuild the affected population from the order's own scope wording - state, line, transaction type and period - without using the remediation team's extract.
Compare your record count and value to the population that was paid and quantify any shortfall.
Check the period used matches the order rather than the examiner's sample window, since a truncated period is the most common understatement.
Treat any understated population as a reportable breach requiring department notification, not a test exception.
testing.done: the restitution population is independently rebuilt and any shortfall against the ordered scope is quantified and reported.

testing.step: Recompute restitution amounts and interest on a sub-sample
actions: Take 30 records from the paid population and recompute the underpayment or overcharge from the source transaction against the corrected rate, form or claim treatment.
Recompute interest using the rate and accrual basis the order or state statute requires from the transaction date to the actual payment date.
Compare to the amount paid and log any record paid short, including short interest, as an exception.
Confirm the control totals tie to the general ledger funding entry.
testing.done: 30 restitution records recompute to the amount paid including statutory interest, tied to the ledger funding entry.

testing.step: Trace payment delivery and the unreachable remainder
actions: Trace 20 sampled records to an issued payment with the restitution reason code, the payment date and the cleared or uncleared status.
Confirm the explanatory letter was sent in the counsel-cleared wording and that the mailing date is recorded.
Test the unreachable remainder for evidence of address search and the escheatment route, and check none was simply written off.
Log any record with no payment, no letter or an undocumented write-off as an exception.
testing.done: sampled payments trace to issued payments with letters, and the unreachable remainder shows search and escheatment evidence.

testing.step: Re-perform the post-change effectiveness sample
actions: For each closed finding, pull 15 transactions processed after the corrective action effective date in the affected state and line.
Test each against the corrected requirement independently and compute your own post-change error rate.
Compare to the error rate the closure package claims and to the tolerance the order states, or 5% where silent.
Treat a finding closed on a claimed rate you cannot reproduce as an exception on closure evidence, regardless of the actual rate.
testing.done: each closed finding has an independently computed post-change error rate compared to the claimed rate and the tolerance.

testing.step: Test root cause quality and the wider-exposure extension
actions: Read the root cause on each sampled finding and confirm it names a control failure supported by data, not a restatement of the finding.
Confirm the wider-exposure assessment covered unexamined states and lines and that corrective actions were applied there too.
Check whether any finding flagged Repeat had a prior root cause that would have prevented it if the earlier action had held.
Log narrow-scoped remediations and unsupported root causes as exceptions, since they are what produce repeat findings.
testing.done: each sampled root cause is evidenced and its corrective action is shown to have reached the unexamined states and lines.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the state, exam year, finding reference and the timeliness, restitution, closure-evidence or scope category.
Assign a root cause and an owner at executive level for anything touching a regulator-committed date.
Open a self-notification assessment with Regulatory Counsel for understated restitution populations and missed committed dates.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, executive owner where a commitment was missed, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time closure rate against regulator-committed dates, the restitution completeness rate and the closure-evidence pass rate.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-tolerance thresholds on committed dates and restitution completeness.
Have the independent reviewer, who designed and signed off none of the sampled corrective actions, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and, where any commitment was missed or a repeat finding exists, to the board risk committee, and file the workpaper under Market Conduct / Exam Remediation.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states on-time closure, restitution completeness and closure-evidence rates with a conclusion and the committee reporting dates.
